name: Route Desk rules
author: Hemanth Vallamkonda
status: Proposed method. Drafted for an application; not tested in a Janus Henderson tenant.
principle: AI drafts and matches. These rules give a first view. The AI Business Partner and the ATC challenge it, and people decide.

problemType.why: Nobody owns the decision. Agree the owner and write the rule down first; a model cannot supply a missing owner.
The inputs arrive in different shapes. Standardise them first (one template or form); a rules-based flow can then take the volume.
Standardise the input first, then let AI handle the variation that remains. The first step is agreeing a template, not building a tool.
Fixed rules on structured data run more reliably and more cheaply in a flow than in a model.
The work is language or judgement, and the pain is volume, scattered knowledge or wording.

tiers.label: Tier 3: full control review
tiers.reviewers: Technology, AI Governance, Information Security and Compliance or Risk review before the build; a named approver for every output; logging on.
tiers.why: Client, personal or market-sensitive data (or data nobody has labelled yet), or output that goes to the board, auditors, regulators or clients, or into a system of record.

tiers.label: Tier 2: checklist review
tiers.reviewers: Technology and the data owner sign a short checklist before the pilot.
tiers.why: Confidential internal data, or output that feeds a team document or decision.

tiers.label: Tier 1: notify only
tiers.reviewers: A register entry on a pre-approved pattern; no review meeting.
tiers.why: Internal, non-sensitive data used in the person's own work.

routes.plain: the capability is not available in-house

routes.plain: it needs core platform integration or writes to a system of record
routes.because: Escalated demand goes to Forward Deployed Engineering.

routes.plain: it is deterministic work on structured data

routes.because: A tested pattern in users' own hands.

routes.because: The Partner builds it and hands it to a Fighter Pilot.

platforms.text: No build yet. Agree the owner, rule or input standard, then re-run the desk.
The tool the firm already owns, if its AI features meet the need. If not, re-run the desk with that answer changed.
Whatever the programme uses. No parallel build.
An Agent Builder or SharePoint agent grounded on content the users can already open, or the firm's own agentic workspace where it is approved for this data.
Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat or another approved tool, with a tested prompt from the Prompt Library.
A Copilot Studio agent with SharePoint knowledge and a citation on every answer.
A Copilot Studio agent with an agent flow for the multi-step parts, or another platform approved for this data class.
A Power Automate cloud flow; a desktop flow only where a system has no API; AI Builder document processing where inputs are scanned documents.
Built by Forward Deployed Engineering on the firm's own agent and data platforms, or as a change to the core system.
A vendor product through the Buy workstream, or a partner build handed over for the firm to own.

gates.text: A named person approves every output before it reaches a client.
A named person approves every output before it goes to the board, auditors or regulators.
AI proposes; a person posts. No direct writes to the system of record.
The reviewer signs off the document, as today.
The user owns the output and reviews it before sharing.

tier3GateAddendum: Logging on, and the control partner samples outputs every month.

people.text: The ATC convenes the decision on the owner or the template. No tool training yet.
The ATC connects the team with the tool's or programme's own champions.
A Fighter Pilot runs a 30-minute show-and-tell and owns the prompt page; the ATC watches usage.
A Fighter Pilot co-builds and owns the agent from go-live; the ATC agrees go-live and runs the monthly benefit check.
The ATC is the business contact; a Fighter Pilot writes the test cases and runs user acceptance.

hours.baseline: Time log on the next 10 instances before anything is built (about two weeks).
hours.pilot: The same log in week 4 of the pilot. Hours saved = (baseline minutes minus pilot minutes) x monthly volume.
hours.confirms: The benefit owner signs the figure.
hours.pitfall: Avoids counting hours at stake, self-reported estimates or tool-estimated assisted hours as hours saved.

quality.baseline: Score 10 recent outputs on a short rubric: accuracy, completeness, tone, edits needed.
quality.pilot: Score 10 pilot outputs on the same rubric, blind to which is which.
quality.confirms: The usual reviewer scores; the ATC keeps the sheet.
quality.pitfall: Avoids judging quality by how the tool feels to use.

risk.baseline: Count the errors or exceptions per month that reach review or leave the team.
risk.pilot: The same count during the pilot, reported as a percentage with the counts beside it.
risk.confirms: The control owner confirms the counts.
risk.pitfall: Avoids a percentage with no denominator.

revenue.baseline: Record the leading measure the idea moves first, such as response turnaround or capacity.
revenue.pilot: Track the leading measure in the pilot; review win rate quarterly with the commercial owner.
revenue.confirms: The commercial owner agrees how revenue is attributed before any is claimed.
revenue.pitfall: Avoids crediting AI with revenue that markets or the sales team earned.

shape.draft: Common shape: publish it as a pattern after go-live; it is likely to recur in other units.
shape.find: Common shape: publish it as a pattern after go-live; it is likely to recur in other units.
shape.judge: Unit-specific rules: reuse the harness (review gate, evidence log), not the prompt.
shape.move: Reusable as a flow template for similar hand-offs elsewhere.

path.one: Person to team: the Fighter Pilot shares the prompt, with its checks, through the Prompt Library.
path.team: Team to other teams: publish the pattern in the Use Case Library.
path.teams: Pilot in one team first, then widen; Technology hardens anything that becomes business-critical.
path.firm: Pilot in one office first, then widen; Technology hardens anything that becomes business-critical.

verdicts.text: Worth it: start with a smaller first slice
Not yet: recheck when a pattern or platform lowers the effort
Park: log it and recheck at the quarterly review

controlAddons.text: DPIA screening with the Data Protection Officer before any personal data is processed.
Compliance confirms information-barrier and insider-list controls (UK MAR) before build.
The data owner labels the source data first; until then it is treated as tier 3.
Oversharing check on the SharePoint sites the agent will ground on: permissions and sensitivity labels reviewed first.
Financial promotion sign-off where the output is marketing; a Consumer Duty check where retail clients will see it.
The accountable owner signs the final version, and that version is kept for the record.
An accountable Senior Manager is named in the register (SM&CR).

environments.text: The tool's or programme's own environment and owner.

Zone 1 (citizen development): personal and team productivity on content users can already access, sharing limited, under the default data policies. The prompt or agent page names a Fighter Pilot as owner.

Zone 2 (partnered development): an IT-managed environment, built as a solution, published with IT-admin approval and moved with pipelines. A named business owner, a Fighter Pilot as co-owner and connections under a service account, so nothing breaks when the Partner rotates.
The process automation team's managed environment and release process, with a named business owner.
Zone 3 (professional development): Technology's production estate, release process and support model.
The vendor's service under contract, with a named business owner and exit terms.

killCriteria: Retire or rework if, by the end of the pilot, verified benefit is below the floor agreed with the benefit owner, or the agreed quality bar on the test set is missed. Record the lesson in the knowledge base either way.
adoption: Adoption is tracked separately as a prerequisite, not counted as value: routine use by the intended users, for example four or more active days in a rolling four weeks.
